subject: biology
guideVersion: Published February2023; May2023 and March2024 updates; current2027 examiner instructions link this version

primarySources.role: Current official examiner instructions identify version

accessNote: Official indexed PDF was accessed through its link from the2027 examiner instructions. Direct-download challenge was not bypassed. No third-party question-bank text or images used.
levelPolicy: sl means shared SL/HL material; ahl means a response actually requires additional higher-level understanding. Difficulty alone never changes tier.

assessment.paper1B: Four syllabus-related data questions across the themes; 1A and1B completed together without interruption
assessment.mcq: One mark each, no deduction for a wrong response
assessment.bookletNote: Do not invent a Biology data-booklet entitlement; provide any formula, table or reference data needed by original practice questions.

markingPolicy: Use original analytic mark points and explicit acceptable alternatives where appropriate.
Separate calculation method, result and biological reasoning when separately assessed.
Our A/M/R codes are portal authoring conventions, not claims of official IB markscheme notation.
Use command terms consistently; explain requires causal reasoning, evaluate requires limitations/strengths, compare requires paired statements.
Data must be sufficient to justify the awarded answer; uncertainty and causal limitations must not be suppressed.
authoringRules: All question wording and markschemes must be original.
Generated images are schematics, never claimed real micrographs or observations.
Use intact axes, units, scale bars and direction labels; do not reveal the tested answer through a caption.
Do not infer statistical significance only from overlapping or non-overlapping unspecified error bars.
Supply critical values and assumptions when asking statistical tests.
Use reliable biology even where a guide simplification or apparent typo could mislead.

topics.title: Water
sharedConcepts: Aqueous origin and medium of life
Water polarity and intermolecular hydrogen bonding
Cohesion, xylem tension and surface habitats
Solvent roles in transport and metabolism
Buoyancy, viscosity, thermal conductivity and specific heat: aquatic versus aerial habitats
additionalHlConcepts: Asteroid delivery of water; retention through gravity and condensation
Liquid water, habitable orbital zone and search for extraterrestrial life
limitsAndExclusions: Origin hypotheses restricted to asteroids; retention restricted to gravity and temperatures allowing condensation
Named organism common or scientific names acceptable
dataAndExperimentalSkills: Represent partial charges and hydrogen bonds between water molecules
Compare physical-property data with biological adaptations

topics.title: Nucleic acids
sharedConcepts: Nucleotide components; schematic phosphate, pentose and base
Antiparallel complementary DNA strands and hydrogen bonds
DNA/RNA strand, base and sugar differences
Near-universal genetic code as ancestry evidence
additionalHlConcepts: Purine-pyrimidine pairs and uniform helix width
Nucleosomes: eight core histones, DNA and linker histone
Chargaff data and falsification of a repeating tetranucleotide model
limitsAndExclusions: SL: do not require recall of purine/pyrimidine lengths or hydrogen-bond numbers
DNA drawing need not be helical
No memorized example of genetic-code conservation required

topics.title: Origins of cells
additionalHlConcepts: Early atmospheric conditions and abiotic carbon chemistry
Catalysis, replication, assembly and compartmentalization as prerequisites
Evidence used to date early cells/LUCA
limitsAndExclusions: Entire subtopic AHL
Distinguish plausible hypotheses from proof; laboratory synthesis of organics is not creation of life
dataAndExperimentalSkills: Evaluate model atmosphere and geological evidence
Distinguish first life from last common ancestor

topics.title: Cell structure
sharedConcepts: Light microscopy preparation, calibration and measurement
Electron microscopy, freeze fracture, cryo-EM and fluorescence
additionalHlConcepts: Repeated origins and advantages of multicellularity
limitsAndExclusions: Bacterial model: Gram-positive eubacteria; detailed unusual prokaryotic variations excluded
Do not present generated artwork as a micrograph
Atypical examples: aseptate hyphae, skeletal muscle, erythrocytes, sieve-tube elements
dataAndExperimentalSkills: Recognition/drawing from legitimate micrographs or explicitly labelled schematics

topics.title: Viruses
additionalHlConcepts: Acellular organization, nucleic acid and capsid
Multiple origins and convergent parasitism hypotheses
Rapid evolution in influenza and HIV
limitsAndExclusions: Entire subtopic AHL
Examples: lambda phage, coronaviruses and HIV; rapid-evolution examples influenza and HIV
Do not imply all viruses contain both RNA and DNA or all are enveloped
dataAndExperimentalSkills: Interpret infection-cycle diagrams, time-series and selection evidence

topics.title: Diversity of organisms
sharedConcepts: Karyograms and human chromosome-2 fusion evidence
Genome variation within and between species
Genome sequencing applications and changing cost
additionalHlConcepts: Asexual reproduction/horizontal transfer challenges to species concept
limitsAndExclusions: Recall chromosome counts only humans46/chimpanzees48; supply others
Dichotomous keys and eDNA are AHL
Simple limitations of species concept can be shared; asexual/HGT detail is AHL
dataAndExperimentalSkills: Classify chromosomes by length, banding and centromere
Construct keys and interpret eDNA at HL

topics.title: Classification and cladistics
additionalHlConcepts: Root, nodes, terminal branches and relationships
limitsAndExclusions: Entire subtopic AHL
Reclassification case-study details need not be memorized
Cladogram branch length represents time/change only when explicitly defined

topics.title: Evolution and speciation
sharedConcepts: Splitting species versus gradual within-lineage change
Reproductive isolation and differential selection, including Congo-separated Pan populations
additionalHlConcepts: Hybridization/polyploidy in plant speciation, including Persicaria
limitsAndExclusions: SL can assess geographical reproductive isolation; named modes and broader mechanisms AHL
Acquired non-heritable individual change is not population evolution

topics.title: Conservation of biodiversity
sharedConcepts: Repeated survey evidence and citizen science
Population growth, overuse, habitat loss, pollution and introduced species
Complementary in situ/ex situ measures and germplasm storage
limitsAndExclusions: All shared
Corrected extinction cases: North Island giant moa; Caribbean monk seal; another locally or regionally relevant extinct species
Ecosystem case: Southeast Asian mixed dipterocarp forest plus another relevant loss
Historical non-human mass-extinction mechanisms outside this subtopic
dataAndExperimentalSkills: Evaluate conservation tradeoffs and methodological bias

topics.title: Carbohydrates and lipids
limitsAndExclusions: All shared

dataAndExperimentalSkills: Recognize sugar rings and steroid structures

topics.title: Membranes and membrane transport

topics.title: Organelles and compartmentalization

Golgi restricted to processing/secretion

dataAndExperimentalSkills: Interpret fractionation or labelled compartment diagrams

topics.title: Cell specialization
limitsAndExclusions: Adult niches: two examples enough
Gamete adaptations limited to humans
Pneumocytes: thin typeI and surfactant secretory vesicles in typeII

topics.title: Gas exchange
limitsAndExclusions: Lungs restricted to mammalian alveolar model
Leaf transverse sections: dicot
Detailed Hb affinity mechanisms AHL
